$comment: Transcribed from docs/routing-table.md v1. This file IS the router's data — Greg edits this directly, no deploy required for new rows. Each row's `tiers` maps stakes.tier -> {path, delivery, quiet_hours_override}. `path` values here are the doc's INTENDED path (pre-Phase-1-collapse); the routing engine (src/server/routing/route.ts) collapses LIB/LLM/LLM+VERDICT to TEMPLATE at runtime and reports both `path` (actual) and `intended_path` (this value) per the Phase 1 brief. `v1_scope: true` marks rows the doc's own "What v1 actually implements" section (Groups A, B, C1-C5, E, G1-G3) covers; `v1_scope: false` rows are transcribed for completeness/review but the engine will not be exercised against them in Phase 1 because no connector will ever produce their event_type (App Store, error-rate, correctness-critical, and no-CI/no-tests detection all require infrastructure Phase 1 explicitly does not build). See the PR description for the full list of flagged gaps.

rows.label: commit pushed to non-default branch
rows.notes: Raw commits are noise; they roll up into A4/A5 summaries

rows.label: commits land on default branch (direct or merge)
rows.notes: Digest line summarizes the day's merged work per project, not per commit

rows.label: PR opened
rows.notes: New work started: <plain gist> — gist generated once (LLM), cached on the in_progress item

rows.label: large merge / phase-milestone-sized change (delta above baseline norm)
rows.notes: The mid-build progress narration — how mid-project apps get storyline, not just status

rows.label: branch/PR crosses stall threshold (default 14d quiet)
rows.notes: Gentle, max once per item per 2 weeks: "still want this?" Feeds Ideas surface

rows.label: activity on a dormant project (any push/PR)
rows.notes: Dormancy inverts novelty: the activity itself is the news

rows.label: build started
rows.notes: Unless it becomes B4/B6, nobody cares

rows.label: build succeeded, deploy succeeded
rows.notes: "Your update went live cleanly." Dormant modifier (A6) upgrades wording, not channel

rows.label: build running > 2x typical_build_seconds
rows.notes: Slow-build watch only matters when someone's waiting on prod

rows.label: build failed (never reached deploy)
rows.notes: LC verdict is usually "nothing users see changed" — that's the sentence that kills the panic

rows.label: build failed matching known_flaky pattern
rows.notes: "The flaky check failed again — usually passes on retry." Never pushes

rows.label: deploy failed, previous version still serving
rows.notes: The signature moment: "Your update couldn't go live. The previous version is still running — users are fine."

rows.label: deploy failed, nothing serving (first deploy or replaced-then-died)
rows.notes: The only build-class event that can break quiet hours, and only at LC

rows.label: deploy on a no-CI/no-test project (pack stack_summary flag)
rows.notes: Modifier row: escalates B2/B6 one path level. NOT mechanically applied in Phase 1 — the pack schema has no structured field for "no CI/no tests" (worked example CAG infers it from free-text stack_summary), and parsing free text deterministically without an LLM is out of scope. Flagged as a gap in the PR description; a candidate fix is a topology.ci_coverage enum in a future schema revision.
rows.reserved_reason: no structured schema field to key off without an LLM

rows.label: health check failing / service down
rows.notes: Uses downtime_translation verbatim
rows.reserved_reason: requires a host connector; Phase 1 ships GitHub only

rows.label: service recovered
rows.notes: Recovery pushes iff the outage pushed. Closes the loop — never leave a red push unanswered. Engine expects context.pairedOutagePushed for this row.
rows.reserved_reason: requires a host connector; Phase 1 ships GitHub only

rows.label: recovered, but pack notes a hidden dependency (e.g. Postgres-as-queue)
rows.notes: Addendum to C2's narration, not a standalone push
rows.reserved_reason: requires a host connector; Phase 1 ships GitHub only

rows.label: DB migration failed
rows.notes: Data events skew critical: schema half-applied is scarier than a bad deploy
rows.reserved_reason: requires a DB connector; Phase 1 ships GitHub only

rows.label: DB resource warnings (storage, connections, compute limits)
rows.notes: Predictive, not reactive
rows.reserved_reason: requires a DB connector; Phase 1 ships GitHub only

rows.label: data-integrity signal on a correctness-critical project (pack flags "wrong > down")
rows.notes: SZD's rule: wrong measurements outrank downtime. Pack-driven override, not tier-driven
rows.reserved_reason: waits on a pack field flagging correctness-critical projects, per the routing doc's own v1 scope note

rows.label: error-rate spike above baseline (when error connector exists)
rows.notes: v1 ships without an error connector; row reserved
rows.reserved_reason: waits on an error-rate connector, per the routing doc's own v1 scope note

rows.label: review status changed (in review / approved / rejected)
rows.notes: Approval and rejection both push
rows.reserved_reason: Group D waits on the App Store Connect / Play connector phase (explicit Phase 1 non-goal)

rows.label: new version live in store
rows.reserved_reason: Group D waits on the App Store Connect / Play connector phase (explicit Phase 1 non-goal)

rows.label: crash-rate trend worsening
rows.reserved_reason: Group D waits on the App Store Connect / Play connector phase (explicit Phase 1 non-goal)

rows.label: beta feedback / TestFlight events (SILD's current mode)
rows.notes: Beta-phase apps: store narration is about testers, not the public
rows.reserved_reason: Group D waits on the App Store Connect / Play connector phase (explicit Phase 1 non-goal)

rows.label: connector auth failed / disconnected
rows.notes: The one event class that always pushes regardless of tier: a silently blind dashboard is worse than no dashboard. (Still subject to the push_threshold=never cap — "a never project can't push, period" per the brief.)

rows.label: source goes stale_suspected (quiet while sibling source changes)
rows.notes: "Your repo looks out of date with what's live — I'm narrating from the host side for now"

rows.label: unmappable events accumulating in the unsorted tray
rows.notes: Weekly at most: "3 events I couldn't match to a project — 30 seconds to sort?" (cadence throttling enforced by the resolution layer, not the router)

rows.label: project X down and Y.consumes includes X
rows.notes: Y inherits an addendum at Y's own tier/delivery. Riders on the X narration or Y's digest, never a separate push.
rows.reserved_reason: Cross-project (serves/consumes) routing is out of the routing doc's own v1 scope; not a per-event decision a single-event pure function can make. Deferred to Phase 2/3 alongside LLM narration.

rows.label: X's in_progress item is named in Y.capability_gaps or blockers
rows.notes: The cross-dot sentence

rows.label: internal-tool X (personal tier) down, X.serves nonempty
rows.notes: Toile's rule: framed by consequence

rows.label: capability_gaps present on a live project
rows.notes: The YOKE drumbeat. Phase 1 renders this as a plain standing line on every digest where it applies — cadence decay (daily -> every 3 days -> weekly) is explicitly out of scope for Phase 1 (brief non-goals: "no capability-gap drumbeat rendering").

rows.label: project quiet N days but tier >= live_small and healthy
rows.notes: "Smith's site: quiet and healthy, as usual." One reassurance line, not silence.

rows.label: weekly retrospective (Sunday digest)
rows.notes: "This week you shipped X, moved Y forward, and Z stayed stalled." Phase 1 composes this mechanically from the week's stored narrations (counts, not prose) — the memory-product framing is a Phase 2 LLM upgrade.

rows.label: mid-build storyline for doc-informed packs
rows.notes: Progress against the hard pieces the pack knows about, in layman's terms
rows.reserved_reason: G4 waits on doc-ingested packs, per the routing doc's own v1 scope note
